$doctrine: This file decides what the fine-tuned image model learns — and, just as much, what it must NOT learn.
WHAT IT LEARNS: who Drew, Mango and Abby are, and how the house draws them. Each character has a
trigger token that appears in every caption showing them. Whatever a caption leaves unsaid is what the
token absorbs, so captions never mention anatomy, faces, permanent wardrobe, or the black-and-white look.
WHAT IT MUST NOT LEARN: the setting, the props, the framing, or how busy the panel is. Rick's sentence
owns all of that. So every caption names its background out loud — the barroom included, described like
any other place — and the crops deliberately mix close-ups, waist-ups, full bodies and two-shots.
THE STYLE TOKEN is separate. SWDINK means the finished house cartoon: a rendered scene with a real
background. It appears only on finished cartoons and on the fully-rendered scene panels — never on a
model-sheet study, whose blank paper and lighter rendering would otherwise become part of what SWDINK
means. Studies still carry their character token, so identity is learned from every image while the
house look is learned only from images that actually have it.
Boxes are [left, top, width, height] in the source image's own pixels. They started as proposals from
detect-figures.mjs and were corrected by eye; `columns` splits an evenly-spaced row into that many crops,
one caption each. `skip` records what was deliberately left out and why — those judgements are the point
of this file, not clutter in it.
